reason: Verbatim match at SetupWizard.java:2184-2190: onQuit() only fetches the session to clear villager previews and then does sessions.remove(quitting.getUniqueId()); there is no plugin.getConfig().set("wizard.step..."/"wizard.arena...", null) and no saveConfig() in the method. I grepped every wizard.* writer in the plugin: the only null-clearing site is showStepDone (lines 1062 and 1064, followed by saveConfig() at 1065), which is the successful-completion path only; the writers are autoSave (1684/1686), autoSaveSilent (1707/1708), start()'s arena-switch resync (229/230) and validateCompletion's bounce persist (1202) — all of which write values, never null. The only reader is start() (240/243), with no expiry, TTL, or age field; savedStep in 1..TOTAL_STEPS with a matching savedArena is restored verbatim at 248-259, so an abandoned session is silently resumed indefinitely. saveexit is the strongest instance: lines 1609-1613 call autoSave() (writing step/arena) and the comment at 1610 explicitly says progress is persisted to be continued later, then the session is intentionally kept (line 2193-2195 confirms closing inventories never clears sessions) — so the keys are by-design resume markers for that path, and the defect is narrower than claimed: there is no cleanup on the paths that end the session without completing (quit mid-wizard, and clearVillagerPreviews-only teardown), and no cap, TTL, or reset of stale entries. No accumulation beyond one step+arena pair per admin UUID exists (config.yml keys are `wizard.step.<uuid>`/`wizard.arena.<uuid>`, overwritten in place), so the "grows with dead entries" impact is bounded by the number of distinct admin UUIDs who ever ran /hilltop setup. The stale-progress hazard is also partially mitigated: validateCompletion (1173-1206) re-checks spawn/mob-spawn/nodes/villagers/shop and bounces to the deficient step with a message, so a stale resume after ArenaResetService cannot proceed to completion silently. Net effect: cosmetic config clutter plus a mild UX surprise (resume banner at an abandoned step), correctly low.
